Automobiles and telegraph communication are common
Law enforcement influenced by political and social connections

surface_summary: The Midnight Masquer, a mysterious bandit, robs high society during Mardi Gras, culminating in the murder of Joseph Maillard. Bob Maillard, the son, is arrested but maintains his innocence. Henry Gramont, a geologist and former Midnight Masquer, investigates and uncovers a criminal gang led by Jachin Fell.
accepted_facts: Joseph Maillard was shot twice through the heart during the Comus ball.
Bob Maillard was found changing out of an aviator's costume shortly after the murder.
Ben Chacherre was found with the stolen loot and the aviator's costume.
Jachin Fell is a prominent lawyer and chess master with mysterious connections.
inferred_conclusions: Bob Maillard was the Midnight Masquer and killed his father accidentally.
Ben Chacherre was the thief who stole the loot but not the murderer.
Jachin Fell is an innocent man caught in the criminal web.
mechanism_description: Jachin Fell masterminded the criminal operations, including the lottery and automobile theft ring, using Ben Chacherre as his enforcer. Chacherre murdered Joseph Maillard during a confrontation at the Comus ball, using the stolen aviator's costume and pistol to implicate Bob Maillard. Fell planted false evidence, including a fabricated oil seepage, to manipulate the oil company deal and protect Lucie Ledanois financially while maintaining his criminal enterprise under the guise of respectability.
delivery_path: Jachin Fell orchestrates the Midnight Masquer robberies using an aviator disguise.
Ben Chacherre steals the loot and the aviator's costume from Gramont's car.
At the Comus ball, Chacherre kills Joseph Maillard using the stolen pistol.
Chacherre frames Bob Maillard by planting evidence and implicating him.
Fell plants false oil seepage to inflate the value of Lucie Ledanois' land.
Gramont investigates, uncovers the criminal gang, and arrests members including Chacherre.
Fell's true role as gang leader is revealed but he is protected by government secrecy.
outcome_result: Jachin Fell is revealed as the criminal mastermind behind the murders and the lottery gang, but is protected by his secret role as a government agent, while Ben Chacherre is arrested for murder.

false_assumption.statement: Bob Maillard was the Midnight Masquer and accidentally killed his father.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Bob was found changing out of the aviator costume shortly after the murder and was known for his wild behavior and drinking. The evidence circumstantially pointed to him as the bandit and murderer.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The real Midnight Masquer was Henry Gramont, and the murder was committed by Ben Chacherre to frame Bob. The costume and loot were stolen and used to mislead investigators.

supporting_points: Found changing out of the aviator's costume shortly after the murder.
Known for drunkenness and wild behavior.
Circumstantial evidence linking him to the crime scene.
His story about the murder was weak and inconsistent.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He had no motive to kill his father and was not the original Midnight Masquer; the real murderer was Ben Chacherre.

red_herrings.description: Henry Gramont was suspected to be the Midnight Masquer and possibly involved in the crimes.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His possession of the aviator costume and involvement in the robberies.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Gramont was the original Midnight Masquer acting to expose the criminal gang and protect Lucie Ledanois.

red_herrings.description: Ben Chacherre was initially suspected of stealing the loot and being involved in the murder.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Found with stolen loot and implicated by fingerprint evidence.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Chacherre was the murderer but acted under Fell's orders; his arrest was part of the larger plan to dismantle the gang.

closed_circle.rationale: All suspects were present at the social events and had access to the victim and the crime scenes; the investigation focused on this limited group.

time_windows: Gramont's absence from home until after midnight
trust_channels: Jachin Fell's influence over police and politicians

inference_path.observation: Bob Maillard was found changing out of the aviator's costume shortly after the murder.
inference_path.correction: He was not the original Midnight Masquer; the costume was stolen from Gramont's car.
inference_path.effect: Bob's guilt as the bandit and murderer is questioned.
required_evidence: The aviator costume found in Ben Chacherre's possession
Witness statement of Bob changing costume after the murder

inference_path.observation: Ben Chacherre was found with the stolen loot and the aviator's costume.
inference_path.correction: Chacherre was acting under orders from Jachin Fell and committed the murder.
inference_path.effect: Chacherre is identified as the murderer, not Bob Maillard.

inference_path.observation: Oil seepage was found on Lucie Ledanois' land.
inference_path.correction: The oil seepage was planted by Jachin Fell to inflate land value.
inference_path.effect: The oil discovery is a fraud to manipulate the oil company deal.
required_evidence: Statement by Jachin Fell admitting planting oil seepage

inference_path.observation: Jachin Fell is a respected lawyer and chess master.
inference_path.correction: He is the head of the criminal gang and lottery operation.
inference_path.effect: Fell's public persona conceals his criminal mastermind role.
required_evidence: Evidence of lottery operations and stolen cars at Gumberts' place

inference_path.observation: Gramont was the original Midnight Masquer.
inference_path.correction: He acted to expose the gang and protect Lucie Ledanois.
inference_path.effect: Gramont is innocent and a key investigator.

inference_path.observation: Jachin Fell's influence prevents his arrest by local police.
inference_path.correction: He is a secret special agent of the Department of Justice.
inference_path.effect: Fell's criminal activities are part of a covert government operation.
required_evidence: Fell's claim of being a special agent
Federal agents' refusal to arrest Fell

inference_path.observation: Ben Chacherre tries to frame Hammond for murder.
inference_path.correction: Chacherre is the real murderer; Hammond is innocent.
inference_path.effect: Hammond's arrest is a frame-up by the gang.
required_evidence: Chacherre's bloodied knife found at the scene

discriminating_test.design: Gramont sends a telegram under Chacherre's name instructing an associate not to destroy a bundle of evidence and to meet him at Houma. He then personally arrests gang members and confronts them with the evidence, including the aviator's costume and pistol. The test reveals the true murderer and the gang's operations by forcing confessions and capturing key members.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals Ben Chacherre as the murderer, Jachin Fell as the gang leader, and exposes the planted oil seepage fraud.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Successful capture and confession of gang members, and recovery of incriminating evidence without alerting the criminals.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given all necessary clues, including the presence of the aviator costume, the stolen loot, the false oil seepage, and the suspicious behavior of key characters. The notes, witness statements, and the discovery of the criminal gang's operations provide concrete evidence. The false solution is clearly presented and refuted, allowing attentive readers to deduce the true mechanism.

anchors.claim: Joseph Maillard was shot twice through the heart
anchors.anchor: Dead," he said, curtly. "Shot twice--each bullet through the heart.

anchors.claim: Bob Maillard was found changing out of an aviator's uniform
anchors.anchor: Five minutes afterward he was found in a near-by room, hastily changing out of an aviator's uniform into his masquerade costume.

anchors.claim: Ben Chacherre was found with the stolen loot and aviator's costume
anchors.anchor: Ben Chacherre, who had stolen the loot and the aviator's costume, was arrested.

anchors.claim: Jachin Fell is a lawyer and chess master with mysterious connections
anchors.anchor: Jachin Fell was a member of the most exclusive New Orleans clubs. He was even received in the inner circles of Creole society.

anchors.claim: The oil seepage on Lucie Ledanois' land was planted by Fell
anchors.anchor: I planted that oil seepage myself--or had it done by men I could trust," said Jachin Fell, calmly.

anchors.claim: Gramont was the original Midnight Masquer acting to expose the gang
anchors.anchor: Yes. One reason was that I suspected someone in society, someone high up in New Orleans, to be connected with the gang; but I never dreamed that you were the man, Fell.

anchors.claim: Ben Chacherre murdered the sheriff and Joseph Maillard
anchors.anchor: Ben Chacherre is charged with the murder of the sheriff of Terrebonne Parish, in which I have clear evidence against him.

anchors.claim: Fell is protected by government secrecy as a special agent
anchors.anchor: I am a special agent of the Department of Justice, employed in that capacity through the efforts of Judge Forester and Senator Flaxman.

anchors.claim: Gramont arrests Memphis Izzy Gumberts and gang members
anchors.anchor: I went out to the Gumberts place on Bayou Terrebonne this morning, arrested Memphis Izzy Gumberts and four other men engaged in operating a lottery.

anchors.claim: The aviator's automatic pistol was used to kill Joseph Maillard
anchors.anchor: The Midnight Masquer had fired two bullets into Maillard. Two cartridges were gone from this automatic.

anchors.claim: Gramont is wounded by Charlie the Goog during the arrest
anchors.anchor: Charlie the Goog lay dead on the floor--a touch of heroic tragedy in his last desperate action; he had got me in the arm.

anchors.claim: Fell threatens Gramont to vote with him on the oil deal
anchors.anchor: I want you to vote with me--and I'm going to put my cards on the table before you.

anchors.claim: Fell admits planting the oil seepage to enrich Lucie Ledanois
anchors.anchor: I planted that oil seepage myself--or had it done by men I could trust.

anchors.claim: Gramont calls the governor to confirm Fell's arrest
anchors.anchor: I called up the governor, and have been told not to arrest him.

anchors.claim: Fell reveals he is a government agent to avoid arrest
anchors.anchor: I have done this by the authority of the United States, in order to apprehend Memphis Izzy Gumberts and other men at one crack.

anchors.claim: Gramont has the evidence to put the lottery business into Federal hands
anchors.anchor: I have secured an abundance of evidence to prove that the lottery gang has extended its operations to adjacent states.

anchors.claim: Fell is arrested as the head of the criminal gang
anchors.anchor: I now call upon you to hold him in custody as a Federal prisoner.

anchors.claim: Lucie Ledanois is made financially secure through the oil deal
anchors.anchor: I shall see to it that you will not be injured because of that signed statement.

anchors.claim: The Midnight Masquer's loot was returned to the owners
anchors.anchor: A number of people have received back property this afternoon--loot the bandit had taken.

anchors.claim: Ben Chacherre tries to frame Hammond for murder
anchors.anchor: They claim I done it----
